_readme: Retrieval-level eval cases for search_blueprint. Scored by agents/uno-bot/scripts/run-retrieval-evals.mjs against GET /debug/blueprint-search — NO model, NO judge, seconds not minutes. Every id below was read out of the live blueprint on 2026-08-19, never guessed. Assertions: expectCellIds (any-of within k), expectAllCellIds (all-of), expectPath/expectScenario (>= minMatches rows carry it), expectTopScoreBelow (absence). Classes: paraphrase | exact-term | structural-name | aggregate | absence. `blocker: true` cases must pass; the rest are diagnostics that report without failing the job.

q: what happens if a tutor cancels less than 12 hours before the session
note: Cell says 'Files the late call-off in the app; removal is immediate'. The query shares almost no vocabulary with it — this is vector's job and keyword should miss.
Before Students Join > Prepare breakout rooms > Lead Tutor ('Creates breakout rooms.'). Near-literal, so it should be easy — a miss here means something is badly wrong.

q: who decides whether a call-off is excused
note: Two cells share identical content across Happy and Late paths — either is correct. A golden set that demanded one would be scoring a coin flip.

q: where do applicants first hear about PLUS
note: Answer is the single word 'Handshake' — a low-information cell that only the breadcrumb makes findable. Watch this one when Phase 2a changes the chunk body.

q: how does a tutor confirm a student actually showed up
note: 'Marks the student present' — the canonical paraphrase case: no term overlap with 'confirm', 'actually showed up'.

q: how and when does a tutor get paid
note: 'Receives a biweekly paycheck.' Query says 'get paid' — synonym, not substring.
A proper noun that is semantically meaningless as a concept. Vector should struggle; keyword should nail it. This is the class the hybrid RPC exists for.
'Zoom/Pencil link + host key stored on session record' — appears in exactly one cell in the whole blueprint. Unambiguous ground truth.
A hyphenated identifier — the shape tokenizers and ILIKE both handle badly. Also the case that would justify pg_trgm if to_tsvector alone cannot rank it.
Tool name living on tech-layer cells. Non-blocking: those cells are near-duplicates of each other, so which one wins is not meaningful.
Four cells with byte-identical content ('PLUS App — Call-Offs tab'). Any one passing is the honest bar; ranking among identical text is noise.
Path NAME, not cell prose. Semantic indexes the breadcrumb so it has a chance; the whole future-state branch was unreachable before paths joined the keyword fan-out. Regression cover for that fix.
A named path inside the 310-cell Goal Setting scenario — it has to beat a very large field of siblings.
Punctuation-heavy name. websearch_to_tsquery and ILIKE treat '(<12h)' very differently — worth watching across Phase 3.

DIAGNOSTIC, not a gate. The corpus has no step- or scenario-level summary rows, so 59 sibling cells compete and none is 'the' answer. Bar is coverage: >=5 of 15 rows from the right scenario. Failing here argues for multi-granularity chunks, not for tuning the ranker.
The stress case: 310 cells, 38% of the corpus, one scenario. Should be easy on coverage and useless on precision — which is exactly the finding to record.

q: what are all the ways a tutor can miss a session
note: Spans call-off, late call-off, swap and fill-in. No single scenario is complete — measures whether retrieval can span, which nothing today is designed to do.

q: how do tutors submit expense reports
note: RETIRED AS A THRESHOLD TEST 2026-08-19, and the reason is the finding. This case used to assert top_score < 0.5. Measured across all 26 cases, the two queries with NO answer scored 0.607 and 0.654 — landing BETWEEN genuine hits at 0.565 ('host key') and 0.647 ('who creates the breakout rooms'). Any floor that rejects the absent pair also rejects six real ones, so no threshold exists, and chunk quality cannot create one: the good cases at the bottom are short cells whose scores depend ON the breadcrumb that de-boilerplating would remove. What retrieval CAN honestly report is corroboration — nothing here matches the blueprint's own words, so only the vector list fires. Whether the bot then declines to answer is a prose question, scored by run-evals.mjs, not here.

Same retirement as BR25. Acuity is retired tooling, so this also guards a real fabrication risk — but the guard belongs in the prose eval, where the rule it protects actually lives. Retrieval's contribution is the honest signal that no keyword or structural retriever corroborated anything.
